title: Fines for liquor sales to underage decoys
summary: In August 2026 the liquor board fined Island Grocery Depot, a Pāʻia fish market restaurant, Flatbread Company and Hāʻikū Market after underage decoys were sold or served alcohol in 2025 stings. In September the department reported that 16 of 19 businesses passed August underage-buyer checks.

timeline.text: Motion to adopt the deputy prosecutor's penalty recommendations: The board voted to fine the company $2,000 on count one and $2,000 on count two, with no penalty on count three.
The board voted to fine the store $1,000 on each of counts one and two, with no penalty on count three.
The department's attorney said a bartender served a drink to a minor decoy, an underage tester, on June 27th, 2025.
Back in open session, the board voted unanimously to fine the business $1,000 on each count.
A member moved to fine the business $2,000 on count one, $3,000 on count two, and nothing on count three.
The store pleaded guilty to all three counts, with no plea agreement.
The department said an 18-year-old decoy bought a 5% alcohol drink at the store on July 8th, 2025.
A cashier checked a 19-year-old decoy's real Hawaiʻi ID and still served her a beer.
On June 27th, 2025, the Department of Liquor Control sent underage decoys into the restaurant.
The board took up accusation 2026-13 against Flatbread Company on Hāna Highway.
The board heard a case against Island Grocery Depot, run by Valley Produce Incorporated.
The board took up complaint and accusation 2026-15 against the owner of Hāʻikū Market.
